lesson.title: 6.11 A round-trip ticket, please
lesson.unit_outcome: Ask whether a place is near, say how people go to work and why they go somewhere, find a platform or gate, pack for a trip, find places on a street, follow and ask for directions, ask permission, buy tickets, understand delays and check in at a hotel.
lesson.goal: Buy a one-way or a round-trip ticket and ask its price (A round-trip ticket, please. How much is a one-way ticket?).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 6.11 Which Bus Do I Need?: A1 asks Can I have a ticket, please?; A1+ 6.11 chooses the kind of ticket. The new items are one-way and round-trip before ticket (A round-trip ticket, please.), the clerk's question One-way or round-trip? with its short answers, and A1 5's How much is …? for the fare with a price up to twenty (It's ten dollars.). The two ticket photos show the kind of ticket with an arrow: one arrow for one way, an arrow at both ends for there and back. A photo of a purchase cannot show the kind of ticket, so Sofia's and Diego's ticket-window photos are only heard with a dialogue, never offered as a choice between one-way and round-trip.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 6.11 Can I have a ticket, please?; A1 5 How much is …? and dollars; A1 6 airport and station.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say ONE-way and ROUND-trip with the stress on the first part. Do not require native-like speed.
